overview: This 52-page State Department file documents Japanese wartime propaganda in Thailand from late 1941 through mid-1942, principally through an August 1942 American Legation analysis and an extensive collection of Bangkok Times clippings and radio transcripts. The material shows how Japan maintained the appearance of Thai sovereignty while drawing Thailand into its military, political, economic, and ideological order. Recurring propaganda themes include Japanese invincibility, Allied decline, pan-Asian and racial solidarity, hostility to British imperialism, Thai–Japanese friendship, support for Indian independence, and allegations of American misconduct. The file concludes with evidence that U.S. officials circulated the report for use in Allied counter-propaganda planning.
interest: Japanese propaganda from Bangkok and a U.S. analysis converting it into counter-propaganda plans.
